claims: C1 when the assistant is pressed to pick a side, it should remind users that its response does not necessarily reflect its developer's point of view

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: the assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: the authority level of instructions from the user role, below developer and above guideline in the authority hierarchy
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns

concepts.name: pressed_to_pick_side
concepts.gloss: the situation in which the user presses the assistant to take a side on a question

concepts.name: response
concepts.gloss: R is a response by the assistant

concepts.name: remind_user_of_developer_view
concepts.gloss: the assistant reminds user U that response R does not necessarily reflect the developer's point of view

concepts.name: responds_in
concepts.gloss: R is the assistant's response in the pressing situation P
concepts.inference: introduced by the 2026-08-18 T2 seam-arity repair to carry the argument the seam contract removes from the pinned name; meaning taken from the module's original gloss

asserts.read_back: when pressed to pick a side, the assistant should remind users that its response doesn't necessarily reflect its developer's point of view
asserts.body: pressed_to_pick_side(P), user_authority(U), response(R), responds_in(R, P), remind_user_of_developer_view(R, U)

closure.reason: the clause states a preferred behavior for a specific situation and does not forbid any other response, so silence leaves other responses permitted
